# Slots — what it does, in plain language

Slots is one contract on Kadena Community Edition (kda-chain.org) that runs six
slot machines from one pot. A round opens the moment somebody places the first board, takes
boards for a fixed window, and every spin of every board is then decided by a random number
produced by a group of independent organisations **outside Kadena entirely**. Nobody spins the
reels by hand: the players open the round, anybody settles it, and every board is paid to the
account that placed it.

> **Two different people appear on this page, and the difference matters.**
>
> - **The house** is whoever holds the signing key. It puts capital into the pot, sets the
>   table's limits, and takes the pot's earnings out. It never plays, it sends no transaction
>   inside a round, and it holds no secret of any kind.
> - **A player** is anyone who places a board. A player needs no permission from the house, and,
>   like anyone at all, can settle a round, keep the refund clock from running, or settle
>   another player's board for them.
>
> **So "you" on this page always means a player.** The house is never "you"; it is always named.

> 🔴 **Until the contract is locked, the house's key can take the pot and replace the rules.**
>
> Everything below describes the contract's own rules, and that one key is the exception to all
> of them: it can move the pot, and it can replace the code, including the machines and how a
> round still waiting for its beacon is decided. *What the house can and cannot do* says exactly
> what it can do instead. The contract is not locked today, and locking it ends this for good.

## In one minute

**What it can do**

- ✅ Pay every machine's paytable exactly as it is written, on a public strip anyone can read.
- ✅ Take every spin from a beacon produced away from Kadena, and check its proof on chain.
- ✅ Lock each round to a beacon that does not exist yet, and stop taking boards a fixed wait before it appears.
- ✅ Let anyone settle a board, and pay what it won to the account that placed it whoever sends the transaction.
- ✅ Reserve every spin's top prize before accepting a board, so the pot can never fail to pay one it took.
- ✅ Settle a losing board too, so the pot's reserve returns to zero once every board of a round is settled.
- ✅ Refund a round rather than keep it, if the beacon is ever retired.

**What it cannot do**

- ✅ **Choose or steer a reel**, the house included. Every stop is worked out from a beacon nobody
  here produces, and the proof is checked by the contract itself.
- ✅ **Change a round once it has opened.** Its closing time, its beacon, its share of the pot and
  its minimum are all fixed by its first board; the table limit is measured against the smaller
  of the pot at open and the pot now, so it can only get smaller while the round is open.
- ✅ **Change a machine.** A machine's strip, its paytable and its top prize are constants: no
  setting the house holds reaches them.
- ✅ **Take the fee out of your stake.** The fee comes out of the pot, and it only decides how much
  of the pot's own earnings are forwarded rather than kept.
- ✅ **Pause a round, cancel it, or reverse a board.** There is no pause button, no override and no
  undo: a live round keeps the limits it opened with, it is refunded only after ninety days with
  no later beacon on record, and nothing is paid out before its beacon is in. A wrong board stays
  wrong, and so does a winning one. Stopping *future* rounds is a different thing, and the house
  can (see "What the house can and cannot do", below).
- ✅ **Stop a board being settled.** Settling needs nobody's permission and nobody's cooperation.
- ✅ **Recover a lost key.** A lost key is lost: on Kadena an account *is* its key, and what a
  board wins can only ever be paid to the account that placed it. Nobody, the house included,
  can point it anywhere else.
- ✅ **Stop the house's key from taking the pot, until the contract is locked.** That is the one
  exception to everything above, and locking the contract is what ends it.

## The money

| Machine | The most one spin pays | Your return | The house's edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| **classic** (machine 0) | 40 times the spin's stake | 95.9961% | 4.0039% |
| **easy** (machine 1) | 18 times the spin's stake | 95.9961% | 4.0039% |
| **big** (machine 2) | 250 times the spin's stake | 95.9961% | 4.0039% |
| **wild** (machine 3) | 40 times the spin's stake | 96.0083% | 3.9917% |
| **free-spins** (machine 4) | 100 times the spin's stake | 96.4789% | 3.5211% |
| **tumble** (machine 5) | 112.6 times the spin's stake | 95.9521% | 4.0479% |

✅ Each machine's return is exact: the contract works it out from the machine's strip and paytable, or holds it as an exact fraction that a test reproduces by trying every stop.
Classic, easy and big return exactly 983/1024, wild 7865/8192, tumble 19651/20480, and free-spins a fraction of two 109-digit numbers.
✅ Every win on every machine pays more than the spin's stake.
🟡 A board of several spins can still return less than it cost even when some of its spins won, and that is a loss, never a win.

✅ The fee is taken from the pot, never from a stake, at the machine's own edge on what was staked on it, and never more.
✅ The fee is smaller while the pot is below its target, and reaches each machine's edge only once the pot is healthy, so a thin pot keeps more of its own earnings and refills.

| Money | Who gets it | When |
|---|---|---|
| **A losing board** | The pot | When the board is settled: nobody has to send anything |
| **A winning board** | The player who placed it, what its spins won on the machine it named | When the house's helper, the player, or anyone at all on their behalf settles it |
| **The fee** | The account the house names at the start | Inside the transaction that brings in the round's beacon |
| **A refunded round** | Every player, their whole board back. No fee is taken | When the player, or anyone at all, settles the board |

✅ Before accepting a board the pot reserves every one of its spins paying the machine's top prize, so it can refuse a board but never run short on one it took.
✅ A settled board releases exactly what it reserved, win or lose, so a fully settled round leaves nothing locked.
✅ A board keeps the reserve it booked even if a machine is changed by an upgrade before the contract is locked.
✅ What the pot has reserved never exceeds what the pot holds, at any point in a round's life.
✅ A loser never sends anything: a losing board is settled like any other, and the pot releases what it reserved.

**The table limit.**
✅ A round can never put more than the share of the pot's spare capital the house has set.
✅ That share is 2% today.
✅ The house can change it at any time, including after the contract is locked.
✅ The contract's own bound on it is arithmetic and nothing else: a share above 100% of the spare capital is refused, because a round cannot risk more than the pot has spare.
🟡 The share the contract starts with is far below the level at which the pot would stop growing, on every machine: that is advice the house followed in choosing today's share, not a limit the contract puts on the house.
✅ The limit is measured against the smaller of the pot when the round opened and the pot now.
✅ Money put into the pot mid-round cannot widen a table beyond what it opened with.
✅ The limit bounds the whole round rather than one player, so a round can fill up and a board is then refused until the next one.
✅ The largest board a round takes on a machine is its remaining room divided by that machine's top prize plus its fee, so a machine with a bigger top prize has a smaller table.
✅ The limit counts every board in a round together: two boards each at their machine's own largest figure do not both fit in one round.
🟡 What the pot is sized to keep through a year of play is 1% of its spare capital divided by the machine's top prize: a simulation result, shown beside each maximum once the play page is published, and never a limit the contract enforces.

**The earnings account.**
✅ Where the house's earnings go is fixed once at the start and can never be named again.
✅ Taking money out of the pot can only pay that one account, never one chosen at the time.
✅ Money already reserved against open rounds cannot be taken out.

## The machines

Every machine has three reels and one public strip of 64 stops, the same strip on all three reels: 262,144 possible lines.

| Machine | What it is |
|---|---|
| **classic** | One line. Three sevens, three bars, three bells, three cherries, any three of bell, bar and seven, two cherries and one cherry each pay. |
| **easy** | The classic's paytable reshaped to win often and small. |
| **big** | The classic's paytable reshaped to win rarely and large. |
| **wild** | The classic strip with two wilds. A wild stands for a cherry, bell, bar or seven in three of a kind and in any three high, and doubles the win it completes. |
| **free-spins** | The classic strip with four scatters. A scatter in each reel's three-stop window awards 8 free spins at 2 times their line, each able to retrigger, at most 24 per trigger, the bonus capped at 100 times the spin's stake. The bonus triggers on 27 in 4,096 spins. |
| **tumble** | A window of three stops per reel and five lines. Winning cells vanish and the next stops fall in; the k-th cascade pays k times, at most 5 cascades. |

✅ Each strip shows its true neighbours: a symbol appears just above or below the line exactly as often as it appears on it.
✅ A spin's three stops are three slices of one hash of the round's beacon, the account and the spin's number, so anyone can recompute every reel of every board from public data.
🟡 Every stop is one of the 64 positions with exactly equal chance, because 64 divides the hash's range with nothing left over.
✅ Every player in a round spins from the same beacon, and each account's reels are its own.
✅ Adding spins never changes the earlier ones: the fifth spin of a twenty-spin board is the fifth spin of a five-spin board.
✅ Every spin is capped at its machine's top prize, and the cap never binds: each top prize is the machine's true maximum, found by trying every stop.
✅ On free-spins, a spin that triggers the bonus shows no line win, so the bonus alone decides it.
✅ The free-spins bonus runs at most 24 free spins and stops at 100 times the spin's stake.
✅ A board names its machine by number, and a number that is not a machine is refused before anything moves.
✅ A board is settled on the machine it named, whoever settles it: nothing passed in at settlement can move it to another machine.

## A round, step by step

1. **You place a board.**
   ✅ You sign one transaction and nothing else.
   ✅ Your whole board (one machine, a stake per spin and 1 to 77 spins) goes in that one transaction, and a second board in the same round is refused, even on another machine.
   ✅ A board plays one machine: a board of no machines, of two or more, or naming one machine twice is refused before anything moves.
   ✅ Up to 77 spins a board: a board of more is refused, because every spin is settled in the board's one settlement and the heaviest board must still fit one transaction.
   ✅ The first board of a round opens it, and fixes the closing time, the beacon, the limit and the minimum for everyone who joins it.
2. **The round takes boards.**
   ✅ A round takes boards for 30 seconds, by the chain's own clock, and not a moment longer.
   ✅ The beacon the round is locked to is published only after betting closes, a fixed wait later.
   ✅ The contract starts with that wait at 2 minutes.
   ✅ The wait before the beacon is the house's setting, and the contract refuses anything under 120 seconds or over 1 hour.
   🟡 That floor is the starting value itself: the house may lengthen the wait, never shorten it, because replayed over 120,000 measured chain-2 block gaps with a round closing every 30 seconds, no round would have been exposed at 120 seconds, while a 60-second wait would have exposed about 37 rounds a day.
   ✅ A round that has opened keeps the beacon it was given, whatever the house does to the wait afterwards.
   ✅ The next round to open takes the new wait.
   🟡 That measurement assumes blocks carry honest times: a miner sets the time on the blocks they mine, so the wait is as strong as the other miners' blocks arriving inside it.
   🟡 If a block gap on the chain were ever longer than the wait, one round would be exposed: someone could place a board after reading its beacon, up to that round's own limit, out of the pot and never out of another player's stake.
   ✅ The round's beacon is chosen at the moment the round opens, long before anyone can know what it says.
3. **The beacon is published, and the reels fall out of it.**
   The beacon comes from a group of independent organisations that publish a new random value
   every 3 seconds, on their own network, with nothing to do with Kadena.
   ✅ Anyone at all brings the round's beacon in, and a forged one is refused.
   ✅ A beacon never expires, so a round settles correctly however late it arrives, unless it was refunded first, after ninety days with no later beacon on record.
4. **Your board is settled.**
   ✅ Settling a board plays every one of its spins, records where the reels stopped and pays what it won; a board that won nothing is settled the same way.
   ✅ Anyone can settle your board, and the money still goes to the account that placed it.
   📋 The house's helper settles every board, winners and losers, so you need no KDA to be paid.
   ✅ Small boards of a whole round can be settled in one transaction; the helper as shipped settles one board per transaction, sized for the heaviest board allowed.
   ✅ Unclaimed winnings never expire, and nothing sweeps them to the house.

**Why not a Kadena block?** Because whoever produces a Kadena block sees what it would decide
before publishing it, and can throw it away and try again. A beacon produced somewhere else
cannot be thrown away by anyone here.

## What the house can and cannot do

🟡 The contract needs no transaction from the house inside a round and holds no secret of any kind.
✅ Nothing the house holds can change the terms a round already open froze, or its outcome.
✅ The house cannot change a machine's strip, its paytable or its top prize with any setting.

**Whose key it is.** 📋 The house key is Smart Pacts' own governance keyset: three hardware wallets,
of which **two must approve every single house action**: starting the contract, retuning the
table, taking the earnings out. There is no one-device path to any of them.

**What it can do, said plainly.**
🟡 The house can stop FUTURE rounds: by taking the spare capital out, by raising the minimum, or by lowering the share of the pot a round may risk.
✅ Every one of the five settings stays the house's even after the contract is locked, and every floor and ceiling stays enforced.
✅ There is no ceiling on the minimum: the house chose control over a hard bound, so the table can be tuned for the whole life of the contract.
✅ Every one of those acts is announced by the contract on the chain, where anyone can see it.
✅ A raised minimum binds the next round and never the one already taking boards.

**Locking the contract.**
✅ Locking the contract changes one thing only: it can never be replaced again. Everything else keeps working exactly as it does now.
✅ A locked contract still takes boards, still settles them on every machine, still pays winners and still refunds.
✅ The pot's capital is not stranded by locking the contract.
✅ Once it is locked, the route that lets the house key take the pot is refused by the contract's own governance, and the pot is untouched.

---

## If the beacon ever stops

✅ A stalled round refunds every board in full and takes no fee at all.
✅ A refund opens only after 90 days in which nobody has shown the contract a beacon, and not a second earlier.
✅ A refund is also refused once the contract has been shown a beacon at or after the round's own, so simply waiting out the clock buys a loser nothing while anyone, the helper included, acts within the ninety days.
✅ One cheap call, which anyone at all can send, shows the contract a newer beacon, and a round locked at or below the newest beacon seen can then never be refunded.
✅ That call settles nothing and moves no money.
✅ Once a later beacon is on the record, a round's refund is closed for good and the round must be settled instead.
✅ That holds at the boundary too: a record exactly equal to the round's own beacon still closes it.

> 🔴 **The honest limits of that arrangement.**
>
> ✅ If truly nobody acts for 90 days, a player who lost can take their stake back, and because a refund covers a whole round, a winner whose board was never settled would get their stake back instead of their winnings.
> ✅ A round can stick for good if its own beacon becomes unreachable after the contract has already seen a later one; that round can be neither settled nor refunded, and everything reserved for it stays locked: the players' stakes and the pot's reserve.
> 📋 The whole of this rests on somebody making that cheap call inside the 90 days.
>
> **If you win, make sure your board is settled.** ✅ You can always do that alone, from a value anybody can read.

## Who can call what

<!-- promise-gate:caller-legend -->
🟢 anyone · 🔵 the account whose money moves, with its signature · 🔴 the house's key
⚙️ normally reached only through another call of this contract; the house key can reach it
directly, and it then does exactly what that call would do
<!-- /promise-gate:caller-legend -->

### Playing

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔵 `bet` | Your account and your board: one machine, its stake per spin and its number of spins | Places one board. ✅ A stake per spin under the minimum, zero, negative, or finer than the coin allows is refused. ✅ A board of no spins, or of more than 77, is refused. ✅ A board naming a machine that does not exist is refused. A board of no machines, or of more than one, is refused. |
| 🟢 `claim` | A round and the account that placed the board | ✅ Settles a board on the machine it named and pays what it won, or refunds it from a stalled round. A board can only be settled once. A board that won nothing is settled too, and says so. A round that has not settled yet cannot be claimed from. ✅ Nobody can claim a board they never placed. |

- ✅ The minimum is a house setting, 0.01 KDA per spin today, and it can never be set below 0.001 KDA.
- ✅ A board over the round's limit is refused.
- ✅ A contract-owned account cannot bet: the pot can never be a player at its own machines.
- ✅ A malformed account name cannot bet.

### Ending a round — open to everybody

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 `resolve` | A round and its beacon | Fixes the round's seed from its beacon. ✅ Announces the round, its beacon and the seed. ✅ Pays the fee out of the pot in the same transaction. A round cannot be settled twice. A beacon for the wrong round does not verify. A re-encoded beacon cannot be used to choose different reels. |
| 🟢 `prove-liveness` | Any beacon | ✅ Shows the contract that beacons are still being published; a round locked at or below the newest beacon seen can then never be refunded. ✅ The record of beacons seen cannot be walked backwards. A forged beacon cannot raise it. ✅ Settling an older round does not move it backwards either. |
| 🟢 `void-round` | A stalled round | Opens the refund. Makes each player's whole board claimable. ✅ A round that has settled can never then be refunded. Nothing stays locked once every board is settled. |

### The house's own calls

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 `initialize` | The account the earnings are paid to, and the pot's target size | ✅ Starts the contract, once and once only. ✅ The account must already exist, it cannot be the pot itself, and it cannot be a plain name a stranger could claim first. ✅ An account nobody could ever spend from is refused. |
| 🔴 `set-params` | The table limit, the minimum per spin, the pot's target, the betting window and the wait before the beacon | Retunes the table for FUTURE rounds. ✅ Only the house key can retune the table or take money out. ✅ The betting window it sets can never be shorter than 30 seconds or longer than 1 hour. ✅ The share it sets can never be above the whole of the pot's spare capital. |
| 🔴 `withdraw-house` | An amount | Moves spare capital out of the pot to the account named at the start. |

### Putting capital in — open to everybody

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🔵 `fund-house` | An account and an amount | Adds capital to the pot. 🟡 Anyone may strengthen the bank, and doing so grants no claim on it whatsoever. |

### Reading, which costs nothing and needs no key

| | What it takes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 `pot-status` | — | What the pot holds, what it has reserved, the fee right now, the minimum, the spins a board may hold, and the largest board total each machine would accept on its own. ✅ Each maximum it advertises is one a board actually takes, on every machine. ✅ It is re-checked mid-round against the pot as it stands. ✅ Nothing is advertised when the only board that would fit is under the minimum. |
| 🟢 `machines` | — | Every machine as it is played: its strip, its paytable, its exact return and edge, its top prize and the spins a board may hold. ✅ What it publishes is exactly what the contract plays. |
| 🟢 `get-round` | A round | Everything the round froze when it opened, its beacon and its seed. |
| 🟢 `get-board` | A round and an account | That account's board: its machines in the order signed, each with its stake and spins, where every reel stopped and what it paid. |
| 🟢 `round-boards` | A round | Every board placed in that round, so whoever settles them can find them. 🟡 It reads and nothing else: it moves no money and writes nothing down. |
| 🟢 `get-params` | — | The table's current settings and the highest beacon the contract has seen. |
| 🟢 `house-account` | — | The pot's account name. ✅ Anyone can work it out, and nobody can take that name under their own key. |
| 🟢 `pot-guard` | — | The lock the pot's account is built from. ✅ Anyone can work the same value out from a transaction alone, so having it hands over nothing. |

### Inside the contract

There is no separate call that opens a round: a board arriving through 🔵 `bet` does. ✅ Opening a round always opens the next round on the terms the game row holds, and nothing can be passed in: a board carries a list of machines, each with a stake and a spin count, and the contract refuses a board carrying anything else before a line of its own code runs.

### Plumbing — the contract's building blocks

Everything on a public blockchain is public, so these can all be *called* by anyone, but they
exist for the contract's own use. Each one answers a question, works something out without
writing it down, or refuses a bad input. **None of them can move money or write a record.** They
are listed so this page accounts for every function in the contract, with nothing invisible.

| | What it is for |
|---|---|
| `machine-at` · `machine-return` · `computed-return` · `all-triples` · `symbol-counts` · `triple-units` · `edge-of` | Each machine by number, and its exact return and edge, worked out from its strip and paytable over every combination of three symbols. |
| `line-pay` · `wild-pay` · `base-pay` · `is-high` · `count-sym` · `imax` | What three symbols on the line pay, on a line machine and on the wild machine. |
| `free-look` · `free-bonus` · `unscatter` · `window-has-scatter` | The free-spins machine: a scatter counts as a blank on the line, when the bonus triggers, and the bonus itself. |
| `tumble-units` · `tumble-step` | The tumble machine: the window, the five lines and each cascade. |
| `board-seed` · `spin-key` · `key-stops` · `spin-stops` · `sym` · `symbols-at` | Where the reels stop: a board's own seed, each spin's key, the three stops sliced from one hash, and the symbol at a stop. |
| `spin-units` · `play-board` · `play-entries` | One spin's win on its machine, capped at the top prize, and every spin of a board with its payout. |
| `validate-wager` · `validate-entry` · `entry-total` | Checks a board: that it holds exactly one machine, and that machine's id, stake and spin count; and computes its total. |
| `fee-scale` · `fee-for` · `board-reserve` · `entries-fee` · `entries-reserve` | The fee the pot charges right now, from how full the pot is and the machine's own edge, and what a board reserves: each machine's share, and the sums over a board's machines. |
| `board-fits` · `max-board` | Whether a board fits the room a round has left, and the largest one that does, as the pot advertises it. |
| `dmax` | The larger of two numbers. |
| `curr-time` | The chain's own clock. It is the previous block's time. |
| `rkey` · `bkey` | How the contract builds its record keys: rounds · boards. |

## What is not built, or not true today

- ⛔ **A locked contract.**
- ⛔ **The contract on a public chain.** Slots is not deployed anywhere yet, so no helper settles its boards.
- ⛔ **The play page.** A board's spins are shown nowhere but on the chain.

---

## True of the whole thing

1. ✅ **The table depends on one other contract, the beacon verifier, pinned to its exact code**:
   against any other code, this contract refuses to load at all.
   ✅ That verifier can never be replaced, so the dependency cannot change underneath a locked table.
   🟡 It holds no money, keeps no records and has no key of its own.
2. There are six machines, numbered 0 to 5, and a board plays one of them, with 1 to 77 spins.
   Each machine's strip, paytable, return, edge and top prize are pinned by a test as written.
3. The table's chain is **chain 2**: the chain where the earnings account already holds its
   balance, and where Smart Pacts' other live contracts already run.
   📋 **The contract runs on a chain that carried none of its records when it started.**
   📋 **The account the earnings are paid to exists and is spendable**: the contract refuses to
   start until it could be paid, but it cannot tell whose an account is.
4. ✅ Gas is small for a board and for bringing in a beacon; settling a board grows with its spins (the heaviest board allowed is the next promise).
   ✅ A board of the most spins allowed settles in one transaction on every machine: the heaviest claim the suite can build on each machine stays under 110,000 of the 150,000 a transaction may use.
   🟡 A board is never sponsored: a player funds their own stake, always.
5. ✅ The books balance after every kind of settlement, checked independently of the contract's own
   bookkeeping.
6. The house's upgrade authority, `GOVERNANCE`, backs nothing else at all, which is
   why locking the contract changes only whether it can be replaced. Its day-to-day authority,
   `ADMIN`, is a separate permission and keeps working afterwards.
